answers.core: I don't know of any way to extend `BaseMaterial3D` (or its child classes) to add this feature. This is because the methods for updating the native shader code are not exposed to scripting.
answers.workaround: It can only be worked around by writing a custom shader material. Not only is this not very accessible, but using a custom shader material is also problematic for those who are importing materials from other programs. For example, I know that Blender imports use `StandardMaterial3D` by default. As far as I know, it would require writing a post-import script to change that.

title: Create and expose a `layers` property on `BaseMaterial3D`
